differences.what: massing: a front about 9.6 m wide of two storeys over a high basement, the north flank receding to a one-storey canted bay
differences.how: T-1888: the 1911 sheet's 22.25 x 9.58 m body on K01, the principal floor 2.2 m and the storeys 3.95 and 3.6 m read through this camera; the front's corners, wall head and water table render within about 2 px

differences.what: the street front's four opening columns, the door in the second from the south (the print turned back)
differences.how: T-1888: front_bays 1.18, 3.50, 5.88, 8.37 m and entrance_bay 2; every window renders on its column within about 5 px

differences.what: every street window segmental-headed under a light hood with a key at its crown, the principal storey's taller than the upper's
differences.how: T-1888: street_front_round_heads (segmental, key) over K06's one-over-one segmental sash, 0.95 x 2.15 m and 0.9 x 2.05 m; sills and crowns within about 5 px

differences.what: the high basement of smooth light ashlar on the front to a water table at the principal floor, the front's brick over it far darker
differences.how: T-1888: K02 Lemont limestone stopped at the principal floor (stone_front.brick_above_m 2.2) and the front's brick toned red-brown apart from the flanks

differences.what: the basement lights under the two north principal windows: tall round-headed windows, about 0.95 m by 1.7 m from about 0.15 m over grade
differences.how: T-1888 placed them on their columns; T-3184: basement_lights head round, 0.95 x 1.7 m at 0.15 m, cut in the stone (ROUND_PLAIN) with their spandrels filled, under a plain plinth; sills, jambs and crowns render within about 6 px

differences.what: the north flank: blank brick from the corner, one window a storey, the round-headed pair over the bay
differences.how: T-1888: north_bays read off this camera at s 6.6 (both storeys) and the pair at s 9.0 and 10.15; they render on the print's

differences.what: the one-storey canted bay of light stone on the north flank, about 9-12 m back from the front
differences.how: T-1888: K08 canted bay, stone, 3.0 m along the wall and 1.2 m proud, its top 5.7 m; its edges render within about 10 px

differences.what: the bracketed cornice round the front and the north flank
differences.how: T-1888: K10's bracketed timber cornice at the 9.75 m wall head, 0.9 m out

differences.what: the low stone wall on the street line before the lawn, no fence on it
differences.how: T-1888: K11's stone coping wall, 0.45 m high

differences.what: the door's height: a tall doorway, its head level with the principal windows'
differences.how: T-1888: door_clear_height_m 3.0 read through this camera

differences.what: the door's segmental stone hood and key over a pair of leaves, as the windows' hoods; built as a plain K07 door in a square hole
differences.how: T-3184: a round-headed doorway 1.4 x 3.3 m over the landing under K01's door arch (a stone ring with its key to 5.85 m) and K07's pair of leaves in a 0.4 m reveal; the ring and key stand on the print's hood within about 8 px

differences.what: the iron balconettes under the two north principal windows (the north one broader, on scrolled consoles); not built: the kit lays a balcony only on a bay
differences.how: T-3184: street_front_iron.balconettes, read off this camera: v 5.36-6.39 m 0.25 m proud, and v 7.20-9.55 m 0.6 m proud on two scrolled consoles, each a pierced iron guard 0.8 m high on a stone slab at the water table; their ends render within about 6 px

differences.what: the stoop's cast-iron railings, scrolled panels on newels, over open steps; built with K07's solid stone cheeks
differences.how: T-3184: entrance_kit cheeks false and street_front_iron.stoop_rails: K11's stoop rail each side, a scrolled panel 0.5 m deep under the handrail, the scroll at the foot

differences.what: a stone belt across the front at the second floor and a thin band at the principal heads, which K01's stone front lays and the print does not show
differences.how: T-3184: stone_front.belts [] - the brick runs unbroken from the water table to the frieze

differences.what: the north flank's basement is light stone in the print, like the front's; built in the flank's common brick to grade
differences.how: T-3184: side_base, the front's stone faced on the north flank to the water table at 2.2 m, round the flank's basement light

differences.what: the bay's lights round-headed, its stone base with a round-headed basement light, and its top a bracketed cornice; built square-headed under a plain cap
differences.how: T-3184: K08's hooded canted bay (a hood on consoles), its lights round-headed (K06 round fanlight sash), the near cheek's 0.8 m wide, and a narrow round-headed light in its 2.2 m stone base; the hood's line within about 10 px; re-rendered after the base light was set on the kit's 0.6 m plinth (0.72-1.92 m) and each cheek's light centred on its cheek, as K08's storey and pier rules require: no change a visitor would notice

differences.what: the cornice's depth: a tall plain frieze with panels between paired carved brackets about 1.1 m deep; K10's cornice is shallower and its brackets smaller
differences.how: T-3184: the eave raised to the print's cornice top (10.85 m), K10's brackets paired and sized 0.8 m deep and 0.7 m out (wall_head.bracket_m), over a plain frieze 0.9 m deep from the wall head; the crown and the brackets' feet render within about 6 px at both corners

differences.what: the basement lights are round-headed in the print; K06's area light is square-headed
differences.how: T-3184: the basement lights are cut round-headed (see above)

differences.what: the walk passes through the stone wall in the print; K11's coping wall is unbroken
differences.how: T-3184: the wall's run ends at s 11.63 m (x 630 px on the street line) and the walk's opening runs on to the north lot line (the K11 coping wall's opening run)

differences.what: the roof: a low hipped roof with a broad centre gable and an oculus over the front, two tall stacks; the 1904 house carries the mansard storey of 1886 the photograph predates (the register; the 1911 sheet's 3 storeys), built reconstructed over the same cornice. A picture before 1886 is evidence of its date (AGENTS.md rule 11), so its roof is not copied into 1904
colour: the print is monochrome; only the front's brick reading darker than its stone and the sunlit flank is read
the south flank and the rear, which the camera does not see
the hoods' short ears at their springing, which K06's band does not carve
the round-headed pair's lights set 0.4 m apart, the kit's least between read windows, where the print shows a narrow mullion

the north wall ends at the bay's far side in the print (sky beyond; the 1911 sheet steps the wall back 1.26 m behind the bay): the print shows the full-height body ending about where the sheet's step is (its cornice to x 984 px, about u 8.5 m) and no wall over the step; the 1904 body runs on to the rear at full height
differences.how: T-3184: the photograph is of before 1886 and the sheet of 1911, which draws a section stepped back there; its height in 1904 is not in any picture held, so the print is evidence of its own date (AGENTS.md rule 11) and the 1904 body follows K01 to the rear (L-k01-1834-jones-1888)

differences.what: the stoop's landing carried south to the front's south corner as a terrace behind a pierced iron guard (x 177-302 px at the landing's height)
differences.how: T-3184: entrance_kit terrace (left, to the corner) and the stoop rails' guard along it, pierced its whole length

differences.how: T-3184: north_bays: the window's head round, and a light 0.5 x 1.45 m at 0.3 m, round-headed; both on the print's within about 6 px

differences.what: the doorway's leaves: dark in the print (in shadow, or open), lighter in the render

differences.what: the iron reads light in the print; K01's iron is dark

differences.what: the frieze's panels between the bracket pairs and the brackets' carving; the frieze is built plain and the brackets are the kit's scroll
